stages.title: Advanced vocabulary and terminology
stages.hook: How can one root such as 'feliz' give you felicidade, infelizmente and felizmente?
explain: Portuguese builds a rich vocabulary through derivation. Suffixes: -mente forms adverbs from feminine adjectives (feliz → felizmente, rápida → rapidamente), -dade forms nouns (felicidade, liberdade), -ção forms nouns from verbs (educar → educação), -ável / -ível means 'able to be' (possível, confiável). Prefixes: in-/im- and des- negate (infeliz, desfazer), re- repeats (refazer).

Many words come from Latin and Greek: biblioteca, democracia, filosofia. Precision matters: 'ao passo que' (whereas), 'a fim de' (in order to), 'em virtude de' (due to). Be careful with false cognates and register: 'obter' is more formal than 'conseguir'; 'iniciar' is more formal than 'começar'.
stages.mnemonic: Root plus suffix: feliz, felizmente, felicidade.
sentences: He did it in order to learn.

gq.why: Adverbs in -mente are built on the feminine form of the adjective: rápida becomes rapidamente.

gq.q: What does the prefix 'des-' usually do?
o: It repeats the action of the verb
It marks the plural of the noun

panel.q: Why is 'iniciar' often chosen in formal writing?
o: It is shorter than começar, so it is formal
It is higher in register than começar
It is slang, used between friends
It is a noun, not a verb
panel.why: Iniciar and obter belong to a higher, more formal register than começar and conseguir.

panel.q: Which word is a noun formed from 'educar'?
panel.why: -ção forms nouns.
A fim de means in order to.

teach.model: Build words with suffixes -mente, -dade, -ção, -ável and prefixes in-, des-, re-. Use precise connectors: ao passo que, a fim de, em virtude de.

stages.title: Academic language
stages.hook: How do you write 'It can be concluded that...' in academic Portuguese?
explain: Academic Portuguese is impersonal and precise. It uses the passive and the impersonal se: 'Conclui-se que ...' (It is concluded that ...), 'Observou-se um aumento' (An increase was observed), 'O estudo foi realizado ...' (The study was carried out ...). Parts of a paper: resumo (abstract), introdução, metodologia, resultados, discussão, conclusão, referências.

Hedging: 'parece indicar', 'pode-se afirmar', 'sugere-se que' (it is suggested that). Connectors: 'Nesse sentido' (in this sense), 'Por conseguinte' (consequently), 'Não obstante' (nevertheless). Citations: (Silva, 2020) in Brazil follow ABNT norms; Portugal commonly uses APA or Portuguese standards. Avoid first person and colloquialisms.
stages.mnemonic: Resumo, método, resultados, conclusão: the shape of a paper.
sentences: The study was carried out in 2020.
It is concluded that the method works.
The results suggest a clear trend.

gq.q: Which section describes how the study was done?

o: The first person, as in 'eu concluo'
To sound casual, like a friend
To shorten the text for the reader
To add colour to the writing
panel.why: Hedging expresses caution.
Por conseguinte means consequently.

o: Brazilian technical standards for academic work
A football club in the south
A bank in the Brazilian capital
panel.why: ABNT is the Brazilian standards body.

teach.model: Use passive and impersonal se: Conclui-se que... Parts of a paper: resumo, metodologia, resultados, discussão, conclusão, referências. Hedge claims.

stages.title: Professional communication
stages.hook: How do you finish a professional email in Portuguese?
explain: Professional communication uses clear structure and polite formulas. Brazilian emails: 'Prezados,' ... 'Segue em anexo o currículo' (Attached is the CV), 'Fico à disposição para qualquer esclarecimento' (I remain available for any clarification), 'Atenciosamente'. Portuguese emails: 'Exmos. Senhores,' ... 'Com os melhores cumprimentos'.

Workplace words: currículo (CV), reunião (meeting), proposta (proposal), contrato (contract), prazo (deadline), orçamento (budget or quote), entrevista de emprego (job interview). In meetings: 'Gostaria de propor ...' (I would like to propose), 'Podemos agendar?' (Can we schedule?), 'De acordo' (Agreed). Keep tone clear and respectful; avoid excessive slang.
stages.mnemonic: Segue em anexo, fico à disposição, atenciosamente.
sentences: We need to respect the deadline.

gq.q: Which closing is formal in Portugal?

o: It is slang used among friends
It is a question about the schedule
panel.why: It is a courtesy formula.

o: Façam a reunião amanhã, sem falta
panel.why: The conditional is polite.
Orçamento means budget or estimate.

teach.model: Open with Prezados or Exmos. Senhores. Use Segue em anexo and Fico à disposição. Close with Atenciosamente (BR) or Com os melhores cumprimentos (PT).

trip.prompt: Read examples of Portuguese business emails.

stages.title: Literary analysis
stages.hook: How can a dead man narrate a novel?
explain: In 'Memórias Póstumas de Brás Cubas' (1881) Machado de Assis uses a narrator who tells his life after death, creating irony and a playful relationship with the reader. In 'Ensaio sobre a Cegueira' (1995) José Saramago imagines an epidemic of blindness and explores human behaviour; Saramago won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1998. Guimarães Rosa's 'Grande Sertão: Veredas' (1956) invents language in the Brazilian backlands.

Poetry: Fernando Pessoa (Portugal), Carlos Drummond de Andrade and Cecília Meireles (Brazil). Tools of analysis: voz narrativa (narrative voice), ironia, metáfora, símbolo, ritmo, tema. Ask: What is the effect of this choice? 'Machado usa a ironia para criticar a sociedade' is an analytical claim; support it with a short quotation and explanation.
stages.mnemonic: Voice, irony, metaphor: ask what effect each choice has.
sentences: The poem has a strong rhythm.

gq.q: Who won the 1998 Nobel Prize in Literature?
What is distinctive about the narrator of Brás Cubas?
o: He is a child telling a story
He is a robot in a future world
He does not exist, so there is no story
gq.why: Brás Cubas tells his story after his death, which makes the narration ironic and playful.

panel.q: Why is irony a useful analytical term?
o: It describes saying one thing and meaning another
It counts the syllables of a poem
It names the setting of a story
panel.why: Irony names the gap between what is said and what is meant, which is central to Machado's style.

panel.q: What should support an analytical claim?
o: A summary only, in your own words
A guess about the author's life
A long copy of the whole page
panel.why: A short quotation with explanation shows that your claim comes from the text.

panel.q: Which question helps interpret a metaphor?
o: What does it compare and why?
panel.why: Asking what the metaphor compares, and why, leads to its effect in the text.

teach.model: Use voz narrativa, ironia, metáfora, símbolo, ritmo and tema. Support claims with short quotations.

points.ask: How do I support a claim?

stages.title: Advanced listening comprehension
stages.hook: How can you follow a fast radio interview in Portuguese?
explain: Advanced listening involves reduced speech, discourse markers and implied meaning. Brazilian speech reduces: 'tô' (estou), 'tá' (está), 'pro' (para o), 'né'. European Portuguese reduces unstressed vowels strongly. News phrases: 'de acordo com' (according to), 'ao que tudo indica' (everything suggests), 'em declarações à imprensa' (in statements to the press).

Strategies: predict the topic, note numbers and names, notice connectors (porém, no entanto, portanto) and tone. Do not stop at each unknown word; keep following the main line. Review with a transcript afterwards. Listening to different accents (Brazil, Portugal, Angola, Mozambique) builds flexibility.
stages.mnemonic: Keep following the main line even when a word escapes.
sentences: According to the minister, prices will fall.
The interview was on the radio.

o: por isso, which marks a cause

panel.q: Why should you keep listening after an unknown word?
panel.why: The surrounding words and topic often make an unknown word clear without stopping.
Hearing Brazilian, European and African speech prepares you for real conversations.
A transcript reveals what you missed.

teach.model: Expect reduced forms: tô, tá, pro. Notice connectors and tone. Predict topics and follow the main line.

trip.prompt: Listen to news from different countries.

stages.title: Oral fluency and presentations
stages.hook: What can you do when you lose a word in the middle of a presentation?
explain: Fluent speakers use fillers and strategies: 'ou seja' (that is), 'digamos' (let's say), 'quer dizer' (I mean), 'como é que se diz?' (how do you say it?), 'por assim dizer' (so to speak). Paraphrase: 'aquilo que usamos para ...' (the thing we use for ...). Self-correction: 'ou melhor' (or rather).

Signposting a talk: 'Para começar', 'Em segundo lugar', 'Para concluir'. Vary intonation, use pauses, and look at the audience. Rhythm differs by variety: European Portuguese reduces unstressed vowels more, so it can sound more compressed to learners. Recording yourself helps.
stages.mnemonic: Ou seja, ou melhor, digamos: tools for gaining time.
sentences: That is, the plan is simple.

o: It shows an error in the speaker
It is only polite to do so
panel.why: Paraphrase keeps the flow.

o: To waste time during the talk
panel.why: Listening back reveals habits such as fillers or recurring errors that you do not notice while speaking.

panel.q: What do pauses do in a talk?
panel.why: Pauses aid comprehension.

teach.model: Use ou seja, digamos, ou melhor, por assim dizer. Paraphrase when you forget a word. Signpost with para começar and para concluir.

points.ask: What if I forget a word?

stages.title: Translation and interpretation
stages.hook: What is the difference between a translator and an interpreter in a conference?
explain: A translator (tradutor) works on written text; an interpreter (intérprete) works on speech. Consecutive interpreting (interpretação consecutiva) happens after the speaker pauses, while simultaneous interpreting (interpretação simultânea) is done in real time in a booth.

Challenges: false friends, idioms, cultural references, register, and different varieties of Portuguese. For a Brazilian audience, say 'ônibus', for a Portuguese one 'autocarro'. Keep terminology consistent using glossaries. Ethical rules include accuracy, impartiality and confidentiality. Explain cultural terms like 'saudade' briefly rather than leaving them unclear.
stages.mnemonic: Written word: tradutor. Spoken word: intérprete.
sentences: The interpreter works in a booth.

o: Interpreting at the same time as the speaker
Written translation of a long text

panel.q: Why adapt vocabulary to the audience's variety?
o: To show off a wider vocabulary
panel.why: Using words such as ônibus or autocarro that the audience expects makes the interpretation sound natural.
Explain cultural terms.

o: It is optional and depends on the client
Clients trust interpreters with sensitive information
It is a rule of style only
panel.why: Clients and speakers share sensitive information with interpreters and must be able to trust them.

teach.model: Translators work with text; interpreters with speech. Consecutive and simultaneous modes. Keep terminology consistent, adapt to the variety, and respect ethics.

stages.title: Idiomatic and figurative language
stages.hook: What does it mean to 'pay the duck' or 'swallow toads' in Portuguese?
explain: Portuguese idioms are colourful. 'Pagar o pato' (to pay the duck) means to take the blame. 'Engolir sapos' (to swallow toads) means to put up with unpleasant things. 'Custar os olhos da cara' (to cost the eyes of the face) means to be very expensive. 'Dar com os burros n'água' means to fail. 'Não ter papas na língua' means to speak frankly. 'Matar dois coelhos com uma cajadada só' is to kill two birds with one stone.

Variety matters: 'quebrar o galho' (Brazil) means to help out, and 'chutar o balde' (Brazil) means to give up in frustration; 'ficar a ver navios' (Portugal) means to be left with nothing. Never translate idioms literally. Match the idea, register and tone.
stages.mnemonic: Pato, sapos, olhos da cara: animals and body parts carry the meaning.
items: dois coelhos com uma cajadada só
sentences: I had to put up with a lot.

o: To buy food for a friend
To pay a fee or a fine
To win a prize in a game
gq.why: It means to bear the blame.

gq.q: Which idiom is used in Portugal for being left with nothing?
o: quebrar o galho, used in Brazil
chutar o balde, used in Brazil
pagar o pato, which means taking the blame
gq.why: Ficar a ver navios is European Portuguese for being left with nothing.

o: They are old and no longer used
They are short and easy to say
They are rude and should be avoided
panel.why: Literal translation confuses.
Quebrar o galho is Brazilian.

panel.q: What should you match when translating an idiom?
o: Only the words, one by one
Only the grammar of the sentence
Only the length of the phrase
panel.why: Equivalence of effect.

teach.model: Learn pagar o pato, engolir sapos, custar os olhos da cara, não ter papas na língua. Some are regional. Never translate literally.

trip.prompt: Look at idioms from both varieties.

stages.title: Extended independent writing
stages.hook: How do you write a 600-word opinion essay in Portuguese?
explain: Plan: tese (thesis), argumentos (arguments), contra-argumento (counterargument) and conclusão. Introduction: hook and thesis ('Defendo que ...'). Body: each paragraph has an idea, evidence and explanation. Counterargument: 'Alguns argumentam que ..., no entanto ...' (Some argue that ..., however ...). Conclusion: restate the thesis in new words and give a final thought.

Style: varied sentences, accurate agreement, and connectors such as 'Além disso', 'Por outro lado', 'Em suma' (in short). Revise for repetition, spelling and accents (por que, porque, por quê, porquê!). 'Por que' asks why; 'porque' gives a reason; 'por quê' ends a question; 'porquê' is a noun. (This is Brazilian usage; in Portugal the question word is usually 'porque' at the start and 'porquê' at the end.) Read aloud to check flow.
sentences: Some argue that it is expensive.
In short, I support the idea.

gq.q: Which word is a noun meaning 'the reason'?

o: Em suma, which closes the text
Para concluir, which closes the text
To add length to the text
To change the topic of the essay
panel.why: A second reading catches repetition, spelling and accent errors and improves clarity.

panel.q: In Brazilian spelling, which form ends a question?
panel.why: Por quê is used at the end.

o: Add a new topic at the end
Ask unrelated questions to the reader
Restate the thesis in new words
panel.why: Conclusion synthesises.

teach.model: Plan tese, argumentos, contra-argumento and conclusão. Use connectors: além disso, por outro lado, em suma. Distinguish por que, porque, por quê, porquê.
